subject: Constrain specific factor theta when plotting item characteristics and information in bifactor model

messages.author: 6a96270785c153ae
messages.subject: Constrain specific factor theta when plotting item characteristics and information in bifactor model
parts:
Hi Phil,

I'm very new to mirt and R, so I've been having difficulty figuring out how to plot easily interpretable Categorical Characteristic Curves and Information Curves for a bifactor model of the data I'm working with. The model is of 21 polytomous (7 categories) items loading onto 7 specific factors (3 items per factor) and 1 general factor. The specific factors are not a focus of the current research project, so I was wondering if it were possible to constrain a given specific factor's theta to 0 and just plot the item characteristics and information for the general factor at that point?

Thanks,
Daniel M.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Constrain specific factor theta when plotting item characteristics and information in bifactor model
parts:
Hi Daniel,

Using the itemplot() function, try passing drop.zeros=TRUE. If your bifactor model has only 2 loadings per item then these 0 terms will be dropped and plotted as a two-dimensional representation. For the full test characteristic functions this strategy unfortunately will not work. 

Phil

parts: On Wed, Mar 28, 2018 at 3:58 PM, Daniel McKelvey <daniel.k...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi Phil,


Thanks for the quick reply. I included the drop.zero=TRUE ("itemplot(BFIRTMRNI, 1, type = "trace", drop.zeros = TRUE)") in the function and it provided a 3-d representation of the curve (attached), which I could not readily interpret. Is it possible to limit the plotting of the specific factor so that it is only displaying the characteristic curve of the general factor at specific factor theta = 0 so that it looks analogous to a unidimensional characteristic curve (attached unidimensional model of the same item) or perhaps over a range from -1 to 1 instead of -6 to 6?

No, that's not really how multidimensional models work. Sorry.
 

Thanks,
Daniel
